notes: CAD via the H.S.T. marker (F14) - and the H.S.T. number itself, 123142812RT0001, is gold-labelled tax_id that no selector below reads. That is registered extraction debt, not a deferral: scorecard.CHECKED_FIELDS asserts it and it fails every run until somebody writes the selector. 70+ sub-account identities (F13). The F8 refusal - 14,789.77 printed against 14,740.85 Please Pay, aging all zero, nothing on the page explaining the 48.92 - derive_amount_payable is wired (Task 11) and correctly REFUSES on this document (F8): total_printed and please_pay disagree with nothing on the page explaining it, so derived.amount_payable is null and payable_basis is null, matching gold. No vendor_name selector, deliberately: the printed name (page 1's very first line, nothing above it to anchor on) is wider than every closed-vocabulary top region can capture without truncation - top-left cuts it at 'U-PAK DISPOSALS(1989)', dropping 'LTD', and every anchor-based alternative either restates the value (the old, now-removed anchor-is-value selector) or cannot reach it (near-anchor/same-row/label-block are all bounded too narrowly or wrongly positioned relative to it). derived.vendor_name is supplied instead by resolve_vendor_alias's DISPLAY_NAMES table (rung 3, 'printed evidence wins where it exists; the table is for where the print is unreadable') - not the table's intended case (the print here IS readable), but the honest outcome given no selector can cleanly reach it. Same remediation GUARDRAIL 9 already uses elsewhere (edco/bill_to_attention, complete_beverage/bill_to_attention): delete the selector rather than ship one that restates its own answer. bill_to_name (Task 6) reads 'NORTHSTAR RECYCLING COMPANY' on the gold PDF, not the full printed 'Northstar Recycling Company LLC': the 'LLC' wraps to its own line 8pt below (this document's local line pitch), 1.5pt past near-anchor's fixed 40pt vertical floor, so it is structurally unreachable without either widening near-anchor globally (out of scope, affects every persona) or switching to label-block, which on this document has no blank line separating the name from the bill_to_address block beneath it and so bleeds the address in instead - tested and rejected. The truncated name still matches the pack roster's bare 'Northstar Recycling' rendering, so bill_to_mismatch does not false-positive. The selector is scope 'block' plus an ANCHORED party-name shape, and both halves were forced by measurement on all 12 real second samples plus the gold PDF. As shipped (pattern 'text_block') it was wrong on 3 of 12: text_block captures the whole left column inside near-anchor's 40pt window, and on '_AP Invoice 4421470' an 'ATTN: SEAN LEES' line (top=161.18) sits between the label and the party (top=169.18), on '_AP Invoice 4489932' an email line (top=165.18) does, and the OCR-sourced 'Large UPAK with AP and AR' returned garbled text. Each blob also cost the record its bill_to_address, because resolve_bill_to_alias derives that via _block_under keyed on the exact printed party string and nothing sits under a two-line blob. Porting windstream.json's shape idiom on its own is WORSE, measured not assumed: with the default scope 'line' near-anchor reaches x=390 from 'Bill' (x0=90) and takes in the 'Location:' service-location column at x0=355.07, whose rows interleave one row above the bill-to rows, so 6 of 12 returned the SERVICE LOCATION ('ROYAL CANIN', 'BLUE ZONE', 'MARS CANADA', 'RED ZONE', 'ARL LAB', 'ASPIRE BAKERY') - wrong-party reads on correctly-addressed bills. scope 'block' is what answers that: it is the path that applies regions.column_cut, which before this branch was reachable only by pattern 'text_block' because executor._candidates dispatched on the literal pattern name (GRAMMAR EXTENSION, section 1.1 - see schema.FieldSelector.scope). The anchored ^...$ shape answers the other half: re matches it against the WHOLE string unless re.MULTILINE is set and compile_restricted never sets it, so a block carrying anything besides the name cannot match at all, and a clean miss falls through to resolve_bill_to_alias's roster rung - which returns 'NORTHSTAR RECYCLING' AND restores bill_to_address. Measured result over the 12 samples plus gold: 10 clean captures, 3 clean misses, zero wrong values, bill_to_address present on all 12, no bill_to_mismatch on any correctly-addressed document, and the false bill_to_mismatch the OCR sample used to raise is gone. The guard stays armed: a U-Pak bill printing a clean single-line party that is not on the roster is still captured and still raises bill_to_mismatch (tests/packs/test_upak_bill_to_name.py). bill_to_address (Task 10) anchors 'LLC' - the gold PDF's own wrapped continuation line, chosen so label-block's skip drops it and captures the two lines below cleanly. DISCLOSED GAP, found by second-round review: this anchor is GOLD-DOCUMENT-SPECIFIC. Checked against all 12 real second-period samples in all-docs/second-samples/u_pak/*.pdf - zero contain the literal word 'LLC' anywhere. One inspected in detail ('_AP Invoice 4421470 U-Pak 1360.60000.pdf') prints its Bill To block as 'ATTN: SEAN LEES / NORTHSTAR RECYCLING / 94 MAPLE ST / EAST LONGMEADOW MA 01028 / USA' - no 'LLC' line at all, and the extra 'ATTN:' line shifts the whole block up one row versus the gold document's layout. This selector therefore adds bill_to_address coverage for the ONE gold document it was built and verified against, and adds none of the 12 known real second samples - it FAILS SAFE on them (ops/infer.py's pre-existing _block_under fallback only runs when this selector does not match, so those 12 documents simply keep whatever fallback behaviour they had before this selector existed - no regression), but a general fix (e.g. anchoring on something universal to the block, or handling the ATTN:-shifted layout) is still open work, not delivered by this change.
